Base directory for this skill: /Users/michaelrihm/Documents/Projects/toolkit-v2/plugins/session-skills/skills/handoff

# Handoff

Voice: write to the owner in plain English. Claude Code: follow the project's Plain English output style. Codex: follow the "How to write replies" section of `AGENTS.md`.
Leave the project ready for a fresh session, then write a checked prompt it
can start from. Never stop the owner from clearing context.

## Steps

Track the steps in the plan tool (Claude Code: task list; Codex: `update_plan`).

1. **Check the project.** No `.toolkit.json` with `"toolkit": "toolkit-v2"`:
   skip steps 2, 3, and 6, say so in one line, and put everything in the prompt.
2. **Update this session's work item**, never one it did not work on:
   Overview, Resume here, stage, one history note, read back.
   `references/update-the-work-item.md`.
3. **Save what must outlast the session:** unsaved "keep this" items and
   unanswered "Save to memory?" questions go to `memory-save`; then replace the
   focus entry "Next session starts with". `references/save-memory-and-focus.md`.
4. **Draft the prompt; do not show it yet.** Fixed first line, goal, why,
   where it is written down, what to read first, unsaved decisions, open
   questions, one first action, a source kind per fact. `references/prompt-format.md`.
5. **Check the draft** with `handoff-verifier`; act on every verdict as the
   table in `references/check-the-prompt.md` says.
6. **Back up** the work items and memory that live only on this computer. Keep
   the one line it prints for step 7.
   `toolkit handoff-backup`
7. **Show the result:** the `session-summary` table first when a recap was
   asked for; the saves and the backup line (anything not saved first); the
   checker's short list; the prompt in one fenced block; the last line
   "Clear the context, then paste this prompt."
8. **"/handoff check"** (Codex: `$handoff check`): only step 5, on a pasted
   prompt (`references/check-the-prompt.md`, "Checking a pasted prompt").

Anything that does not follow this path (no work item, a refused stage move,
a failed save, a second `/handoff`, no check wanted): open
`references/edge-cases.md`.

## Gotchas

- The prompt's first line is fixed, word for word, on every prompt: "This
  handoff prompt is AI-generated and may contain hallucinations, skewed
  context, etc. Please evaluate accordingly."
- Saves come before the prompt. Once the prompt is on screen, the owner treats
  the session as over and the saves get skipped.
- Skip the check and the prompt carries this session's guesses as settled
  facts. Run it, or say inside the prompt that it did not run.
- Update only a work item this session worked on. Another session may own an
  open item, and this handoff would overwrite its Overview and Resume here.
- Save the focus with `--expect <version>`, never without. Without it, a save
  drops another session's change without a word.
- Never delete a claim the checker marked `Unchecked`. Label it "not
  confirmed" inside the prompt.
- A failed save never blocks the prompt. Lead with "Not saved" (the write
  failed) or "Saved but not verified" (the read-back failed), name the write,
  and carry its content in the prompt.
- The backup never blocks the prompt. A failure line, or "No backup folder
  is set", goes first in the saves list with what it asks the owner to do
  (`references/edge-cases.md`).
- A GitHub Issues or Jira tracker makes `toolkit work` exit with code 3.
  Follow `references/tracker-github.md` or `references/tracker-jira.md`.
- Never commit `.memory/` or `.work-items/`. A save that changed a Git-tracked
  document (for example `DECISIONS.md`) goes through `publish-docs`.
- Run each `toolkit` command alone, on its own line, in both hosts, reads
  included: `cat .toolkit.json && toolkit work show WI-001 --path` is two
  commands. Text goes on standard input in Claude Code and in
  `--text '<text>'` in Codex (`references/toolkit-commands.md`).

## Opening another skill

- Claude Code: the Skill tool with the skill's name, for example
  `memory-save`.
- Codex: read that skill's `SKILL.md` from the path in the skill list, then
  follow it.
- Not installed: say so in one line and carry on without it.

## What this skill is not

- Not a recap. `session-summary` answers "which of my requests are where".
  When the owner asks for both, this skill runs and shows the
  `session-summary` table first (step 7).
- Not the resume. The next session's briefing shows "Next session starts
  with"; `work-on` opens the item by id and rechecks its state and approvals
  before acting.
- Not a hook. The session-end event fires on a clear, but it cannot stop the
  clear or tell the agent anything, so the owner starts this skill.

## References

| File | Open it when |
| --- | --- |
| `references/update-the-work-item.md` | Step 2: finding the item, the Overview and Resume here text, stage, history note, read-back |
| `references/save-memory-and-focus.md` | Step 3: memory saves and the "Next session starts with" entry |
| `references/prompt-format.md` | Step 4: the parts of the prompt, source kinds, an example prompt |
| `references/check-the-prompt.md` | Step 5, step 7's short list, and "/handoff check" |
| `references/edge-cases.md` | Anything that does not follow the normal path: no work item, a refused stage move, a failed save or backup, a second `/handoff`, no check wanted |
| `references/agent-handoff-verifier.md` | Step 5 in Codex: the checker's full text for a native worker (copy of `agents/handoff-verifier.md`) |
| `references/toolkit-commands.md` | Before the first `toolkit` command: one command per call, text in a command, exit codes |
| `references/work-item-format.md` | Step 2: section names, changing one section |
| `references/recording-owner-answers.md` | Step 2: an owner decision this session has not recorded |
| `references/tracker-local.md` | Step 2 with a local tracker |
| `references/tracker-notion.md` | Step 2 with a Notion tracker |

2	# Running `toolkit` commands
3	
4	Purpose: how to run a `toolkit` command in Claude Code and in Codex, how to
5	pass text in one, and what each exit code means. Every skill that runs a
6	`toolkit` command follows this file.
7	
8	## Contents
9	
10	- Running toolkit commands
11	- Text in a command
12	- Exit codes
13	- Reporting a save
14	- Reading output and updating what you read
15	- Right and wrong examples
16	
17	## Running toolkit commands
18	
19	- Put each `toolkit` command on its own line and run it as a plain command,
20	  in both hosts. Do not join it to another command with `&&`, `;`, or a pipe,
21	  and do not wrap it in `$(...)`, a loop, or a script. This holds for read
22	  commands too: `toolkit work decisions && toolkit work show WI-001` is two
23	  commands, run one after the other.
24	- Why, in Codex: the project's command rule (`.codex/rules/toolkit.rules`)
25	  runs a `toolkit` command outside the sandbox only when it is the whole
26	  command. A `toolkit` command joined to anything else (`&&`, `;`, a pipe, a
27	  heredoc, `cd ... &&`) or run from a script (for example Python's
28	  `subprocess`) runs inside the Codex sandbox. The sandbox blocks Notion, the
29	  local Hindsight server, and the main checkout's `.work-items/` and
30	  `.memory/` from a worktree, so the command fails or reports the wrong
31	  cause.
32	- The one thing a Claude Code command may carry is its own text on standard
33	  input (`--set-file -` with a quoted heredoc; "Text in a command", below).
34	- Five commands ask the owner first, in both hosts, because they are hard or
35	  impossible to undo: `toolkit machine-setup`, `toolkit memory delete`,
36	  `toolkit memory import`, `toolkit import`, and
37	  `toolkit hindsight service install` or `start`. Get his yes in the reply
38	  before you run one. The host then asks him to confirm the command (Claude
39	  Code: a permission prompt; Codex: an approval). That prompt is expected, not
40	  an error.
41	- When the host refuses one of the five without asking him (Codex with
42	  approvals off: "approval required by policy, but AskForApproval is set to
43	  Never"), say that the cause is that approval setting, show him the exact
44	  command to run himself in a terminal, and wait. Do nothing in its place
45	  that he did not ask for: a refused delete is not a retire.
46	- In Codex, run each of those five alone, with `sandbox_permissions` set to
47	  `require_escalated` and a one-line reason. The approval alone keeps the
48	  command inside the sandbox, where it fails: `toolkit memory delete` cannot
49	  reach Hindsight or Notion, `toolkit machine-setup` cannot write `~/.codex`
50	  or `~/.local/bin`, `toolkit hindsight service install` cannot write
51	  `~/Library/LaunchAgents`, and `toolkit import` from a worktree cannot write
52	  the main checkout.
53	- Write `--json` and `--host` after the command words
54	  (`toolkit memory delete <key> --owner-approved --json`). The toolkit refuses
55	  those five commands when a flag comes first, because the ask-first rules
56	  would not match them.
57	- Never change a work item or a memory record with a script or a shell write
58	  (Python, Node, `sed -i`, `cat >`, `tee`, `cp`). Use the `toolkit` command
59	  that owns it. The hooks refuse the shell write, so it only wastes a step.
60	- `toolkit help <command>` prints every option of one command.
61	
62	## Text in a command
63	
64	The shell changes text before the command sees it. Inside double quotes it
65	runs anything between backticks and anything in `$(...)` as a command, and
66	puts that command's output in the text. The command then saves the text with
67	those parts missing and still reports success. So:
68	
69	- **One-line values** (`--note`, `--effect`, `--append-row`, `--title`,
70	  `--reason`, `--quote`, `--evidence`, `--description`, `--source`): put them
71	  in single quotes, in both hosts. Inside single quotes the shell changes
72	  nothing. Never use double quotes for text.
73	- **An apostrophe inside single quotes:**
74	  - Claude Code: write it as `'\''`, for example
75	    `--note 'Owner said: "it'\''s ready, ship it"'`.
76	  - Codex: write it as ’ (the curly apostrophe, U+2019), or reword the text.
77	    Never `'\''` in Codex: the command rule does not match that form, so the
78	    command runs inside the sandbox, and the tool call can drop the
79	    backslash, which leaves a quote that is never closed.
80	- **Section, design, focus, glossary, and memory text in Claude Code:** pass
81	  it on standard input with `--set-file -` (or `--body-file -` for a memory
82	  save) and a quoted heredoc. The quotes around `EOF` in `<<'EOF'` stop the
83	  shell from changing anything in the text, and no file is left anywhere.
84	  Claude Code refuses `rm` outside the project, so a temporary file there
85	  could never be deleted. Write the command, then the text, then a line
86	  holding only `EOF`:
87	
88	  ```text
89	  toolkit work edit <id> --section 'Overview' --set-file - <<'EOF'
90	  <the whole section text>
91	  EOF
92	  ```
93	
94	- **The same text in Codex:** a heredoc runs the command inside the sandbox,
95	  so do not use one. Give short or medium text in single quotes
96	  (`--text '<text>'`; newlines inside the quotes are kept). For longer text:
97	  1. Make a new folder for this one save with `mktemp -d`. Its name is
98	     unique, so two sessions or two projects never share a file.
99	  2. Write the file in it with the file edit tool (`apply_patch`).
100	  3. Run the `toolkit` command alone, with the file's full path.
101	  4. Delete the file and the folder right after the command succeeds
102	     (`rm <file>`, then `rmdir <folder>`), before you ask the owner anything.
103	
104	  Never write the file and run the `toolkit` command in one shell command.
105	
106	  ```text
107	  toolkit work edit <id> --section 'Overview' --text '<text>'
108	  toolkit work design <id> --text '<text>' --status proposed
109	  toolkit memory focus --text '<text>' --expect <version>
110	  ```
111	
112	- Never use a fixed file name such as `/tmp/wi001-requirements.md`. Every
113	  project starts at `WI-001`, so another session's save could land in this
114	  item.
115	- Never leave a draft file inside `.work-items/` or `.memory/`. A second
116	  `DESIGN.md`-shaped file there confuses the design lookup, and a stray note
117	  in `.memory/` is read as a memory.
118	
119	## Exit codes
120	
121	`toolkit help work` prints them as: "0 ok, 1 error, 2 validation failure or a
122	refused gate, 3 not supported for this tracker, 4 not a toolkit project."
123	`toolkit help memory` uses the same numbers: "1 error or not found, 2 refused
124	(a rule or a stale --expect), 3 not supported by this backend".

# Running `toolkit` commands

Purpose: how to run a `toolkit` command in Claude Code and in Codex, how to
pass text in one, and what each exit code means. Every skill that runs a
`toolkit` command follows this file.

## Contents

- Running toolkit commands
- Text in a command
- Exit codes
- Reporting a save
- Reading output and updating what you read
- Right and wrong examples

## Running toolkit commands

- Put each `toolkit` command on its own line and run it as a plain command,
  in both hosts. Do not join it to another command with `&&`, `;`, or a pipe,
  and do not wrap it in `$(...)`, a loop, or a script. This holds for read
  commands too: `toolkit work decisions && toolkit work show WI-001` is two
  commands, run one after the other.
- Why, in Codex: the project's command rule (`.codex/rules/toolkit.rules`)
  runs a `toolkit` command outside the sandbox only when it is the whole
  command. A `toolkit` command joined to anything else (`&&`, `;`, a pipe, a
  heredoc, `cd ... &&`) or run from a script (for example Python's
  `subprocess`) runs inside the Codex sandbox. The sandbox blocks Notion, the
  local Hindsight server, and the main checkout's `.work-items/` and
  `.memory/` from a worktree, so the command fails or reports the wrong
  cause.
- The one thing a Claude Code command may carry is its own text on standard
  input (`--set-file -` with a quoted heredoc; "Text in a command", below).
- Five commands ask the owner first, in both hosts, because they are hard or
  impossible to undo: `toolkit machine-setup`, `toolkit memory delete`,
  `toolkit memory import`, `toolkit import`, and
  `toolkit hindsight service install` or `start`. Get his yes in the reply
  before you run one. The host then asks him to confirm the command (Claude
  Code: a permission prompt; Codex: an approval). That prompt is expected, not
  an error.
- When the host refuses one of the five without asking him (Codex with
  approvals off: "approval required by policy, but AskForApproval is set to
  Never"), say that the cause is that approval setting, show him the exact
  command to run himself in a terminal, and wait. Do nothing in its place
  that he did not ask for: a refused delete is not a retire.
- In Codex, run each of those five alone, with `sandbox_permissions` set to
  `require_escalated` and a one-line reason. The approval alone keeps the
  command inside the sandbox, where it fails: `toolkit memory delete` cannot
  reach Hindsight or Notion, `toolkit machine-setup` cannot write `~/.codex`
  or `~/.local/bin`, `toolkit hindsight service install` cannot write
  `~/Library/LaunchAgents`, and `toolkit import` from a worktree cannot write
  the main checkout.
- Write `--json` and `--host` after the command words
  (`toolkit memory delete <key> --owner-approved --json`). The toolkit refuses
  those five commands when a flag comes first, because the ask-first rules
  would not match them.
- Never change a work item or a memory record with a script or a shell write
  (Python, Node, `sed -i`, `cat >`, `tee`, `cp`). Use the `toolkit` command
  that owns it. The hooks refuse the shell write, so it only wastes a step.
- `toolkit help <command>` prints every option of one command.

## Text in a command

The shell changes text before the command sees it. Inside double quotes it
runs anything between backticks and anything in `$(...)` as a command, and
puts that command's output in the text. The command then saves the text with
those parts missing and still reports success. So:

- **One-line values** (`--note`, `--effect`, `--append-row`, `--title`,
  `--reason`, `--quote`, `--evidence`, `--description`, `--source`): put them
  in single quotes, in both hosts. Inside single quotes the shell changes
  nothing. Never use double quotes for text.
- **An apostrophe inside single quotes:**
  - Claude Code: write it as `'\''`, for example
    `--note 'Owner said: "it'\''s ready, ship it"'`.
  - Codex: write it as ’ (the curly apostrophe, U+2019), or reword the text.
    Never `'\''` in Codex: the command rule does not match that form, so the
    command runs inside the sandbox, and the tool call can drop the
    backslash, which leaves a quote that is never closed.
- **Section, design, focus, glossary, and memory text in Claude Code:** pass
  it on standard input with `--set-file -` (or `--body-file -` for a memory
  save) and a quoted heredoc. The quotes around `EOF` in `<<'EOF'` stop the
  shell from changing anything in the text, and no file is left anywhere.
  Claude Code refuses `rm` outside the project, so a temporary file there
  could never be deleted. Write the command, then the text, then a line
  holding only `EOF`:

  ```text
  toolkit work edit <id> --section 'Overview' --set-file - <<'EOF'
  <the whole section text>
  EOF
  ```

- **The same text in Codex:** a heredoc runs the command inside the sandbox,
  so do not use one. Give short or medium text in single quotes
  (`--text '<text>'`; newlines inside the quotes are kept). For longer text:
  1. Make a new folder for this one save with `mktemp -d`. Its name is
     unique, so two sessions or two projects never share a file.
  2. Write the file in it with the file edit tool (`apply_patch`).
  3. Run the `toolkit` command alone, with the file's full path.
  4. Delete the file and the folder right after the command succeeds
     (`rm <file>`, then `rmdir <folder>`), before you ask the owner anything.

  Never write the file and run the `toolkit` command in one shell command.

  ```text
  toolkit work edit <id> --section 'Overview' --text '<text>'
  toolkit work design <id> --text '<text>' --status proposed
  toolkit memory focus --text '<text>' --expect <version>
  ```

- Never use a fixed file name such as `/tmp/wi001-requirements.md`. Every
  project starts at `WI-001`, so another session's save could land in this
  item.
- Never leave a draft file inside `.work-items/` or `.memory/`. A second
  `DESIGN.md`-shaped file there confuses the design lookup, and a stray note
  in `.memory/` is read as a memory.

## Exit codes

`toolkit help work` prints them as: "0 ok, 1 error, 2 validation failure or a
refused gate, 3 not supported for this tracker, 4 not a toolkit project."
`toolkit help memory` uses the same numbers: "1 error or not found, 2 refused
(a rule or a stale --expect), 3 not supported by this backend".

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | Done. | Read back what you wrote before you report it as saved ("Reporting a save", below). A "Note:" line in the output still needs action: report it to the owner, or do what it says. |
| `1` | Error, or the record was not found. | Read the message. It names the cause and usually the fix. Do not run the same command again unchanged. |
| `2` | Validation failure, a refused gate, or a stale `--expect`. | Fix what the message names and run the command again. A refused gate means an approval is missing: ask the owner for it. Never work around a refusal. |
| `3` | Not supported for this tracker or memory backend. | For a GitHub or Jira tracker, the message prints the path of the written instructions for that tracker. Follow them to make the same change on the issue. |
| `4` | Not a Toolkit V2 project. | Skip every work item and memory step and say so in one line. To set the project up, open the `project-setup` skill. |

`toolkit: command not found` means this computer cannot reach the command.
The `project-setup` skill fixes that.

## Reporting a save

- Save each settled answer before moving on, then read it back. A command
  that exits `0` is not proof by itself.
- A write failed: lead the reply with "Not saved". Name what was not saved
  and where it should go, and keep the text so it can be saved later.
- "Saved but not verified" in the output means the write happened and the
  read-back failed. The message names the first part that differs. Lead the
  reply with "Saved but not verified", say which part, and read the record
  back to judge it.

## Reading output and updating what you read

- Add `--json` when you need to read the output field by field, for example
  a record's `version`.
- `--expect <version>` tells the command which version of a record you read.
  The command refuses the save (exit `2`) when the record changed since then,
  so you never overwrite a newer edit. Read it again, merge, and save with the
  new version. `toolkit memory focus`, `toolkit memory glossary`, and
  `toolkit memory save` take it. `--expect absent` says it must not exist
  yet: a new record, or a project with no focus yet.

## Right and wrong examples

1. Two reads.
   - Wrong: `toolkit work list && toolkit work show WI-004`
   - Right: `toolkit work list`, then, as a second command,
     `toolkit work show WI-004`.
2. A history note that quotes the owner, with an apostrophe in his words.
   - Wrong: ``toolkit work history WI-004 --note "Owner said: it's ready, `ship it`"``
     (double quotes: the shell runs the words between the backticks as a
     command and saves its output in their place).
   - Right in Claude Code:
     `toolkit work history WI-004 --note 'Owner said: "it'\''s ready, ship it"'`
   - Right in Codex:
     `toolkit work history WI-004 --note 'Owner said: "it’s ready, ship it"'`
   - The prefix is `Owner said:`, which has no apostrophe to escape.
3. Section text in Codex.
   - Wrong: `cat > /tmp/overview.md <<'EOF' ... EOF && toolkit work edit WI-004 --section 'Overview' --set-file /tmp/overview.md`
     (one shell command, a heredoc, and a fixed file name).
   - Right: `toolkit work edit WI-004 --section 'Overview' --text '<text>'`
4. A change to a work item's header.
   - Wrong: `sed -i '' 's/^stage: .*/stage: 04-solution-design/' .work-items/WI-004/WORK-ITEM.md`
   - Right: `toolkit work set WI-004 --stage 04-solution-design --note '<why>'`
5. Toolkit commands from a script.
   - Wrong: `for id in WI-001 WI-002; do toolkit work show $id; done`
   - Right: `toolkit work show WI-001`, then `toolkit work show WI-002`, each
     as its own command.
